The Gaussian lemma's Statement applies its intertwiner clause to “two one-mode Weyl systems” without requiring regularity, but Proof 4.1 passes through a Bochner integral, whose cited [F5] requires strong measurability. A nonmeasurable discontinuous character χ of R² twists the Schrödinger system to another system with the same Weyl relation; the identity intertwines that system with itself, while its Gaussian matrix coefficient χ(v)〈W₁(v)ψ,ψ〉 is nonmeasurable near zero, so the claimed weak average need not exist. Totality instead lets one choose v with nonzero overlap, then Wₐ(−v)η∈M has nonzero reference-line projection. This is a local proof gap; the stated irreducibility claim remains readily provable.
